preview.note: The link stream itself: same encoder, resolution, bitrate, GOP and OSD as what goes over the air. Only radio effects (packet loss, MCS) are missing. Live settings (Image tab, bitrate) show at once; settings that restart the video reconnect by themselves.
nc.local.title: Connect to the board
nc.local.step1.html: Plug the board's USB into this PC without the WiFi adapter and power it up. It boots into debug mode and ADB appears after ~15 s.
nc.local.step2.html: Pick the device above and press Connect.
nc.local.note.html: In debug mode the video link is off, so settings are saved and used on the next FPV boot. Or use the board's WiFi hotspot (hold BOOT 2 s) and pick WiFi hotspot above.
nc.usb.title: Connect over USB
nc.usb.step1.html: Plug the board's USB into this PC (or an Android phone with an OTG cable) without the WiFi adapter and power it up. It boots into debug mode after ~15 s.
nc.usb.step2.html: Press Connect and pick the board (Rockchip / rkfpv) in the browser's list.
nc.usb.note.html: Only one program can use the board at a time: if adb runs on this PC, run adb kill-server first. Everything works over USB, including installing the board scripts, IQ files, recordings and the live picture. Disconnect lets go of the board again.
nc.usb.first: First time on Linux or Windows
nc.usb.linux.html: Linux: a normal user may not open USB devices. Run once, then replug the board:
nc.usb.windows.html: Windows: the board's ADB interface needs the WinUSB driver (the Google USB driver, or Zadig → WinUSB). If Connect says access is denied, install it and replug.
nc.hs.title: Connect over the board's WiFi
nc.hs.step1.html: Power the air unit with its WiFi card. After boot, hold the BOOT button for about 2 s: the card becomes a WiFi hotspot named rkfpv-XXXX.
nc.hs.step2.html: Join that WiFi on this device. If the phone says it has no internet, choose stay connected (or turn mobile data off).
nc.hs.step3.html: Come back here and press Connect. Chrome asks to allow access to devices on the local network: allow it.
nc.hs.note.html: Settings, the live picture and recordings all work over the hotspot. Hold BOOT again to go back to FPV. Install this page (browser menu → Install app / Add to Home screen) while you have internet; it then opens without internet on the hotspot.
boot.title: Boot mode
boot.note.html: What the board does at power-up. Auto: debug mode (ADB) when a PC is on USB, otherwise FPV.
hs.title: WiFi hotspot
hs.note.html: Hold the board's BOOT button for about 2 s (after boot has finished) and the WiFi card becomes an access point: join it, then change settings, watch the live picture and download recordings without USB. Hold BOOT again to go back to FPV.
install.title: Board scripts
install.note.html: Copy fpv, S99fpv and wfb.sh to the board (until the next image is flashed).
image.title: Image (ISP)
image.note.html: Changes apply live while the video runs. iq keeps the value from the IQ file. For FPV, the settings that matter most are, in order: the longest exposure (motion blur), temporal noise reduction (ghosting on fast moves), the gain cap (noise at night), and the AE delay (bright to dark). Change one setting at a time and compare.
iq.title: IQ file (sensor tuning)
iq.note: The stock files are never changed. Edits go to a copy in /userdata/iq; every replaced version is kept, and a custom file that does not start falls back to stock automatically.

boot.confirmFpv:
Always FPV: the board starts the video link at every boot, even with a PC attached.

ADB will NOT come up any more. To undo you need SSH over the wfb link or the serial console ('fpv mode auto').

live.tuneNote: These change the picture as you move them. More on the Image and Video tabs.
radio.txNote.html:
Each card keeps its own level (OpenIPC scale 1–63, about 0.5 dB per step), so swapping cards never over-drives the new one. 8812AU: raw power index. 8812CU / 8822CU / 8812EU: level ÷ 2 = dBm. auto = the card's default (20 / 20 / 40).
Never transmit without an antenna. High levels, especially on the 8812EU, need a solid 5 V supply and cooling: a brown-out reboots the board mid-flight.
radio.linkNote.html: Settings tagged link must be changed on the ground station too, otherwise the link is lost.
